title: Pullback preserves finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ be a
bounded constructible
complex of finite Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Then $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ is bounded constructible and has
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Consequently $Lf^*$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, which is clause (i) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary at the finite coefficient stages.

proof.text: The coefficient ring A is finite by finite_coefficientExtensionRing. The intrinsic bounded-constructibility hypothesis supplies finite support of homology. Choose lower and upper bounds c,d for that support; the interval [min(c,d),d] is ordered and contains it. Apply finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to obtain an etale bounded constructible object L and an isomorphism from its intrinsic comparison to K. Convert the finite-value etale constructibility predicate to the source-library constructible-sheaf predicate degreewise; convert cohomology vanishing to the standard t-structure bounds. The reverse conversion uses [min(c,d),d], so even a zero complex and disjoint bounds cause no difficulty.

Let P be the exact etale inverse image of L along f. The proved source-library lemma boundedConstructible.mapDerivedCategory_upperStar gives bounded constructibility of P. Build the natural isomorphism between intrinsic comparison followed by constant-ring pullback and etale inverse image followed by intrinsic comparison: first whisker openSquarePullbackModel, cancel the intrinsic realization equivalence with its unit, and apply comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso. Descend it by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, then compose its component with the pullback of the origin isomorphism. This gives comparison(P) isomorphic to the specified pullback of K; all coefficient maps are canonical, and sfFiniteDerivedPullback itself is unchanged.

Apply comparison_torAmplitudeIn_iff to L, which is bounded below by its bounded constructibility. The composition isomorphism for derived functors identifies its displayed comparison functor with finiteCoefficientIntrinsicDerivedComparison. Tor amplitude is invariant under isomorphism directly from its quantified representative definition: compose the representative isomorphism with the inverse object isomorphism. Thus the assumed intrinsic Tor amplitude of K reflects to the same etale interval for L.

Use hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn to express etale Tor amplitude in the standard derived tensor t-structure. Apply the proved source-library torAmplitudeIn_leftDerivedUpperStar: its proof chooses a flat complex supported in [a,b], takes exact termwise inverse image, preserves flatness by upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat, and computes the resulting Tor interval on that model. Its derived-functor isomorphism identifies the result with P. This is the blueprint flat-model argument on the etale side, with the interval unchanged.

P is bounded below, so comparison_torAmplitudeIn_iff on X transfers its Tor interval to its intrinsic comparison. Transport it along the isomorphism of step 2. The essential-image implication of finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin on X gives intrinsic constructibility and an interval of homology vanishing for that same pulled-back object; its nonzero homology support is a subset of the finite integer interval. These give the conjunction in sf_pullback_torAmplitude. Finally unpack the witness interval in finiteTorConstructible, apply this conjunction, and reuse the identical endpoints for sf_pullback_finiteTorConstructible.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ be a
bounded constructible
complex of finite Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Then $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ is bounded constructible and has
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Consequently $Lf^*$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

proof.text:
Bounded constructibility is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible], which also
gives that the cohomological interval is preserved. For the Tor bound apply
[lem-sf-flat-model] to $K$: there is an isomorphism $K\cong P$ in
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ with $P$ a bounded complex of flat
$A_Y$-module sheaves, $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. By
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] one has
$Lf^*K=f^{-1}K\otimes_{f^{-1}A}^LA$, and $f^{-1}A=A$; since inverse
image is exact the map $f^{-1}P\to f^{-1}K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and
$f^{-1}P$ is a bounded complex of flat $A_X$-module sheaves, hence
K-flat, so $Lf^*K\cong f^{-1}P$ by [def-weil-derived-tensor]. The
inverse image of a flat sheaf is flat, as follows:
$f^{-1}G'\to f^{-1}G$ is injective
for an injection $G'\to G$ by exactness, and inverse image commutes with
tensor products of module sheaves, so
$f^{-1}F\otimes_Af^{-1}G'\to f^{-1}F\otimes_Af^{-1}G$ is the functor
$f^{-1}$ applied to $F\otimes_AG'\to F\otimes_AG$, which is injective
because $F$ is flat; flatness is understood as in
[lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat]. Hence for every sheaf $N$ of
$A_X$-modules in degree zero the complex
$Lf^*K\otimes_A^LN\cong(f^{-1}P)\otimes_AN$ has terms only in degrees
$[a,b]$, each term $f^{-1}P^q\otimes_AN$ lying in degree $q$ because
$f^{-1}P^q$ is flat. Therefore
$\mathcal H^r(Lf^*K\otimes_A^LN)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ for every such
$N$, which is the finite Tor amplitude of $Lf^*K$ in $[a,b]$ in the
sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
